title: Starting town: what feels flat

notes.heading: Undifferentiated ground
notes.text: Open ground is right for a poor start, but no shared compacted court, dusty approach or settlement edge joins the Hall to it.

notes.heading: Repeated board-like reserves
notes.text: Identical green-rimmed diamonds read as objects laid on sand. Transport and wall reserves have a different abstract marker language.

notes.heading: Weak contact, not no shadow
notes.text: The wooden Hall has a base and contact shading. Its patch does not become a lived-in doorstep or forecourt; shadow alone will not solve this.

notes.heading: Mixed projection and detail
notes.text: Distant canyon relief looks photographic/perspective, while the Hall uses an oblique game view. Sand grain also feels large beside the shack.

notes.heading: No spatial hierarchy
notes.text: The bare gaps dwarf the small Hall. Keep the same anchors; use a restrained lane and localized palm shade to organize space, not add owned buildings.

notes.heading: HUD dominates the first read
notes.text: The town is small beside the upper panels. Art needs better interior emphasis before a separate HUD or camera redesign is considered.

footer: Actual isolated start: Hall level 1, 22 empty sites, no completed wall. A still image cannot prove lack of movement; code inspection supplies that finding.

title: Level 50: what stays flat

notes.heading: Town floor barely develops
notes.text: Strong buildings and stone wall still sit on almost the same sandy canvas as the start. No neighborhood ground/court system carries prosperity.

notes.heading: Streets read as linework
notes.text: Textured surfaces exist, but Fit makes them narrow and uniform. They dodge rectangular controls rather than connect through believable doorstep aprons.

notes.heading: Isolated building plinths
notes.text: Sprites already have foundations and shading. Independent bases and weak generic contact beds remain disconnected from the surrounding town floor.

notes.heading: Perspective wall / oblique town
notes.text: Returns taper into distance while buildings stay similar-sized. The near gate and foreground wall become visually outsized; art alignment is still draft.

notes.heading: Decoration is punctuation
notes.text: A few isolated palms, lamps and pots decorate gaps, but do not form shaded courts, planted groups or a connected public-space hierarchy.

notes.heading: No whole-town focal rhythm
notes.text: Roof details are bright and busy while civic ground stays quiet. The wall reads as one object enclosing many separate pictures, not a metropolis.

footer: Synthetic ideal fixture: all 23 compatible sites level 50. Not owner progress, not a production population. No motion inferred from a still capture.
